Update, 5:39 p.m. ET: Apple has also released the fifth public beta of macOS 26.6 (25G5065a).

Apple is rolling out the fifth developer beta of macOS 26.6. Here's what to expect

macOS 26.6 lacks user-facing new features

Since the first beta of macOS 26.6, it has been clear that this update falls into the "bug fixes and routine improvements" category rather than a release packed with user-facing features.

Nevertheless, given that Apple itself has acknowledged that AI-driven security vulnerabilities have prompted it to accelerate the rollout of security patches, this system update is expected to include additional fixes, some of which are already present in macOS 26.5.

One change Apple specifically called out in the first beta is a fix for macOS deprecation prompts that appeared in some apps after being incorrectly identified as supporting only Intel processors. The company has since also flagged that it has addressed issues with the ecosystem and HealthKit, but has shared few details about this update.

The fifth beta of macOS 26.6 carries build number 25G5065a, which most likely means the next build will be a release candidate (RC).

How to install the fifth beta of macOS 26.6

Here's how to install the fifth beta of macOS Tahoe 26.6:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • From the drop-down menu in the top-right corner, select "macOS Developer Tahoe Beta"
  • Click "Done"
